transactions.title: Rental — one transfer primitive, carrying a term
transactions.what: The holder transfers right #14 to the renter with `expires_at = 1792800000` (2026-10-24). Title does not move: the renter holds the week until that timestamp, after which it reverts with no return transaction.

transactions.title: Sale — the same primitive, no term
transactions.what: The holder transfers right #15 to the buyer with `expires_at = None`. The holding chain collapses to the buyer alone: title moves and the seller keeps no claim.

transactions.title: Transfer without issuer approval — rejected on chain
transactions.what: Identical to the sale above, submitted with the issuer's authorization entry removed. The holder signed it and paid the fee; the contract refused it. Verification is enforced in the contract, not suggested by the interface.
transactions.failure: The contract rejected this transfer because a required authorization was missing. A transfer needs both the holder's signature and the issuer's approval.

transactions.title: Issuer attempting to seize a held right — rejected on chain
transactions.what: The issuer builds, signs, and pays for a transfer of right #16 from its holder to itself. It can supply its own approval; it cannot supply the holder's authorization. Approving transfers never becomes the power to take one.
transactions.failure: The contract rejected this transfer because a required authorization was missing. A transfer needs both the holder's signature and the issuer's approval.
